pr_body:
@eiriktsarpalis testing `Process.Responding` using a real unresponsive process would be very hard (or even close to impossible) to do properly 

I think that we just test the implementation to ensure that #36768 is not coming back

My motivation is that the implementation just checks if a boolean flag is set and calls WinAPI:

https://github.com/JeroenOortwijn/runtime/blob/c4d3ed52ed8c3763ab69dbc53376eca77e02abd4/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/src/System/Diagnostics/Process.Win32.cs#L275-L302


Fixes #40703

issue_context.title: Add tests for System.Diagnostics.Process.Responding
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/38385 added a test for `Process.Responding`, which however was disabled since it depends on the current implementation characteristics of Wordpad.

We should replace it with a test that consistently reproduces the behaviour.
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @eiriktsarpalis
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
No, the PR referenced in #40703 relied on wordpad behaviour to produce a non-responsive process.

@eiriktsarpalis thanks!

FWIW the commit that removed the test: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/38385/commits/c4d3ed52ed8c3763ab69dbc53376eca77e02abd4

review_comments: Any particular reason you removed the old tests -- were they flaky? They did at least verify the public properties.

I've renamed the test and refactored it (moved the common logic to a separate method).

But if it's not obvious when you look at the code then it's likely that I've tried too hard with the refactor and it does not add any value?

I wonder if you are trying to hard - it is a bit hard to read. Also, in the old test, we would always verify that MainWindowTitle turned to something other than empty (it should really test it's not null either) whereas now, depending on timing of process.MainWindowHandle turning non null, it may not read the public property at all because it will never enter the while loop?

If the old tests were stable, would it make sense to keep them but also extend them to read the field as well?
